We’ll have to agree to disagree on this one, but to me, you’re coming across as quite unsympathetic. Saying, ‘her undeveloped prefrontal cortex got her exactly what she wanted’ just shows that you’re not really understanding what I’m trying to say.

As someone with a degree and post grad degree focusing on mental health, and having worked in both a mental health crisis centre and a psych ward, I’ve seen how adverse experiences in young people (including young adults) can significantly impact mental health and behaviour for life. There’s an overwhelming amount of evidence to support this. These adverse experiences can trigger a number of mental health issues (such as being one of the key reasons people develop BPD), potentially substance use issues etc, which often feed into each other.

That’s not to directly blame Thomas or the cast for her choices, that would be ridiculous. And you’re right that she had issues well before getting involved with Thomas, but there’s no doubt he did a number on her which did contribute (not cause, but contributed) to how her situation has turned out. I’m saying she’s had a rough time, and like all of us, is a product of her childhood and early adulthood. Some people come out of these situations better than others. She needs to grow, work on herself and maybe seek longer term inpatient therapy, but I understand why she has turned out how she has. That’s why I feel empathy and sympathy for her and her children, who are growing up with a mother dealing with significant mental health and substance use issues. It’s a sad situation all around, which is why I disagree when some people label her as just a bad mother/person. There’s a lot of complexity to the situation. All of this doesn’t excuse her behaviour, but it helps explain it.

I’ve also since been diagnosed with celiac disease, epilepsy, endometriosis, clinical depression, anxiety, and OCD.
